An adverbial clause is a group of words which plays the role of an adverb. You can use adverbial clauses to be precise about time and place.
Major athletes are popular wherever they go.
Until we meet again, I will be waiting.
Once I get paid, I will write you a check.
I see the same people wherever I go.
Major athletes are popular wherever they go.
Anywhere I go in Boston it's football, football, football.
People will stop talking football as soon as the season is over.
They always come in and eat pasta before a game.

An adverb of time states when something happens or how often.
An adverbial clause of time often starts with one of the following subordinating conjunctions: after, as, as long as, as soon as, before, no sooner than, since, until, when, or while.

For example:
After the game finished, we all went out for drinks. Drop by my house as soon as you've finished your homework.

An adverb of place states where something happens. An adverbial clause of place often starts with a preposition (e.g., in, on, near) or one of the following subordinating conjunctions: anywhere, everywhere, where, or wherever.

For example:
In a galaxy far, far away, there lived a young boy. I like to meet new people wherever I go.
The Simple Past vs. The Present Perfect
When you use time clauses stating with after, when, until, as soon as, once, and by the time, the Simple Past refers to past time and the Present Perfect refers to future events.
I've heard various stories from my servers,   I've met some alright.
Have you met any famous athletes?
You must have met some, right?
I had one group come in and refuse to pay.
They thought since they were sports stars the bill would be free.
I have taken a celebrity's order before.

You often hear the Present Perfect being used to in introduce recent events and then the Simple Past is used to give details.

For example: The space shuttle has reached the space station safely. It delivered fresh supplied to the astronauts living there.

Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self Assessment.
Peter, Amy and Vanessa chat about the sport's culture in Boston.
Instructions: Listen to the definition on the left. Click on the correct box in the table. There is only one answer per audio.
You have 2 attempts to submit your answers.

images.text:
Amy: This is an amazing place you picked, Vanessa.
Vanessa: Thanks.
Amy: Excuse me. I have to take this call.
Peter: Until we meet again, I'll be waiting.
Vanessa: Things seem to be going well.
Peter: They are. We're having a lot of fun together. By the way, Can I borrow $20?
Vanessa: You still owe me $20 dollars from a month ago.
Peter: Once I get paid, I will write you a check.
Vanessa: Right. Say, look at that crowd of people over there. Isn't that Tom Brandy the quarterback of the Boston professional football team?

Peter: Yep. There's his supermodel wife Ginelle too. Man, what an entourage! There must be 20 people in that group. Look at the staff falling over themselves to serve them. It's unseemly.
Vanessa: Major athletes are popular wherever they go.
Peter: But in Boston it's worse!
Vanessa: It's a big sports town.
Peter: I want to go where they are not talking football 24/7. Anywhere I go in Boston it's football, football, football.
Vanessa: People will stop talking football as soon as the season is over.
Amy: What did I miss?
Peter: You missed seeing the great Tom Brandy.
Amy: Oh, I love Tom Brandy. He is so handsome and suave. Have you met any famous athletes, Vanessa? You must have met some, right?
Vanessa: Oh, yeah. I've met some alright.
Peter: Who's the worst?
Vanessa: I can't say who the worst are specifically, but some are very self-entitled. Once, I had one group come in and refuse to pay. They thought since they were sports stars the bill would be free.

Amy: What did you do?
Vanessa: I got their handlers to pay.
Amy: Nice. Who are the best?
Vanessa: I've heard various stories from my servers, but generally, the best sports athletes are the hockey players.
Amy & Peter: Really?
Vanessa: Yeah, they always come in and eat pasta before a game.
They may look like hooligans with their faces battered and bruised, but they are always gentleman. They dress well and they tip the best. I've had the best experiences with them.
Peter: Yeah! Well, too bad their teams stinks!
Amy: Peter. You are incorrigible.
